coordinates.locator: Piano di Emergenza Esterna INFN-LNGS, ed. 2024 rev. 7, pp. 27-28 (A24 chainage of the laboratory's doors) and the A24 tunnel line of OSM way 24389234 (src:geo-lngs-osm-tunnel-relation): midpoint of the doors' stretch, 6142 m from the Assergi portal (km 117,653); same point as geometry:lngs-hall-b
coordinates.note: Approximate, about ±400 m (derived, not surveyed): the laboratory's entrance (km 124,150) and exit (km 123,440) doors are published as A24 chainage; subtracting the Assergi portal chainage (km 117,653) puts them 6497 m and 5787 m along the tunnel, and the midpoint of that ~700 m stretch is taken as the underground complex. The tunnel line's own length (10 187 m) agrees with the plan's chainage (10 176 m). Hall B's own position within the stretch, and the order of Halls A, B and C along it, are not published, so all three halls share this point. Replaces the Assergi street-address point (42.4189343, 13.5183438), which is the surface office complex 6.1 km away. Labelled `campus`/approximate, as for the other detector sites placed from a building or tunnel position rather than a published hall survey (A17 reserves `underground_lab` for rank <= 7 sources; the plan is a rank-9 prefecture document).
coordinates.quote: L’ingresso ai laboratori si trova al km 124,150, quello di uscita al km 123,440.

depth.note: Average rock coverage of the underground laboratory as a whole.
depth.quote: The 1400 metre-rock thickness above the Laboratory represents a natural coverage that provides a cosmic ray flux reduction by one million times

name: LNGS Hall B
notes: No official coordinate for the underground halls was published on any LNGS page fetched. The coordinate recorded is the LNGS address point at Assergi taken from the laboratory's own "How to reach LNGS" page; the underground halls lie under the Gran Sasso massif several kilometres away along the motorway tunnel, so precision_m is deliberately large and confidence is approximate.

summary.plain: One of three big rooms carved out of the rock under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy, about 100 metres long. The ICARUS liquid-argon detector stood at its northern end from 2010 to 2013.
summary.technical: Underground experimental hall of LNGS, about 100 x 20 x 18 m under ~1400 m of rock; the ICARUS T600 plant occupied a 15 x 42.5 m area at the northern end from 2010 to 2013.
